headline: New Zealand's central bank surprised markets by holding rates instead of raising them, knocking the kiwi down about 1.5%. Today brings the UK Budget, the Bank of Canada and the Federal Reserve decision.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar held near a two-week high, about 102.4 on the dollar index, through the Asian session. The Federal Reserve decides at 1:00 PM CT today; a hold is all but certain, so what chair Kevin Warsh says about a December hike will set the dollar's direction.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation near 3.7%, and markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold today and raise rates in December, which supports the dollar. Strong US figures on Tuesday, led by a jump in consumer confidence, lifted the dollar for a third day. What changed: Little overnight. The dollar index stayed near 102.4, its highest since mid-October, and the 10-year US Treasury yield sat close to 5%. Futures still put the chance of a hold today at about 91%. The dollar gained most against the New Zealand dollar after that country's central bank skipped an expected hike. What it means: With a hold priced in, the decision itself should barely move the dollar. What counts is whether Warsh keeps a December hike clearly on the table and whether any officials vote to hike now; a firm message lifts expected US rates and draws money into the dollar, a softer one lets it slip. The question to keep asking: does the Fed sound set on a December hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US goods trade figures at 7:30 AM CT, then the Fed decision at 1:00 PM CT and Warsh's press conference at 1:30 PM CT. US third-quarter growth and the Fed's preferred inflation measure follow at 7:30 AM CT Thursday.

scenarios.base: The Fed holds and keeps December open; the dollar index stays near 102 to 102.6 into Thursday's growth and inflation figures.
scenarios.bull: Warsh signals a December hike is close to settled, or some officials vote to hike now; short-term yields rise and the index pushes toward 103.
scenarios.bear: Warsh plays down December; hike bets fade and the index slips back toward 101.7.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro was flat near $1.113 overnight after five straight days of losses, with no euro-area news. Coming up: German consumer mood at 2:00 AM CT, the Fed this afternoon and the European Central Bank decision on Thursday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The euro has been weighed down by France's debt and budget fight and by costly imported energy, though a European Central Bank hike in December is widely expected. What changed: Nothing new for the euro overnight; it held near $1.1129 as the dollar stayed firm before the Fed. What it means: The euro is waiting on two central banks. A firm Fed today would keep the pressure on, while a clear signal from the ECB on Thursday that December's hike is coming would give it support. The question to keep asking: does the ECB stay firm on December despite France's troubles?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Germany's GfK consumer mood survey at 2:00 AM CT and a German government bond sale this morning, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. The ECB decides at 8:15 AM CT Thursday, with President Christine Lagarde's press conference after; euro-area growth and inflation figures follow on Friday.

scenarios.base: The euro stays near $1.11 to $1.12 as investors wait for the Fed and the ECB.
scenarios.bull: A softer Fed, or Lagarde keeping a December hike firmly on the table, lifts the euro back above $1.12.
scenarios.bear: A firm Fed and a cautious ECB push the euro toward $1.105, especially if French bond worries return.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound was flat near $1.331 before Chancellor John Healey presents his first UK Budget at about 7:30 AM CT. Dealers expect slightly more government borrowing; a bigger jump could unsettle UK bonds and the pound.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation is running well above target, so markets expect the Bank of England to raise rates on November 5, which supports the pound; the government's borrowing plans are the main worry. What changed: No UK figures overnight, and the pound held near $1.3307. Ahead of the Budget, a Reuters poll of the banks that deal in UK government bonds expects this year's bond sales to rise only a little, by about £3.4 billion, with fewer long-dated bonds than in the past. What it means: If the Budget's borrowing comes in close to that, UK bond markets should stay calm and the pound can go back to trading on the rate gap with the US. A surprise jump in borrowing would push UK bond yields up for the wrong reason, worry over debt, which usually weighs on the pound. The question to keep asking: does the Budget calm or rattle UK bond markets?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Healey's Budget statement at about 7:30 AM CT, with the government's bond-sale plans published alongside, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. The Bank of England decides on November 5.
numbers: Dealer poll: this year's gilt sales +£3.4bn to ~£249.6bn

scenarios.bull: Lower-than-expected borrowing or bond sales calm UK bonds; the pound recovers toward $1.335 to $1.34.
scenarios.bear: Borrowing well above expectations lifts UK bond yields for the wrong reasons; the pound drops below $1.325.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The yen was little changed, with the dollar near ¥157.8 after briefly touching ¥158. A firm Fed today could push it higher, but Japan's finance minister has warned Tokyo is ready to step in to support the yen.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The yen sits low because Japan's rates are far below other major economies' and the country pays for costly imported energy; a Bank of Japan hike in December is widely expected but not yet signalled. What changed: Nothing new overnight. The dollar edged up to about ¥158 in Asia and then eased back to near ¥157.8 as Asian stocks rallied. What it means: The rate gap with the US still pulls the yen down, and the Fed's message today could widen it. Tokyo's warnings act as a brake near these levels, where it has bought yen before. The question to keep asking: how close is Tokyo to buying yen?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Fed at 1:00 PM CT, then Tokyo consumer prices at 6:30 PM CT tonight. The Bank of Japan decides on Friday, Japan time (Thursday night CT), with new forecasts; a hold is expected.
numbers: Bank of Japan Oct 30: hold ~98%; December hike ~83–88%

scenarios.base: The dollar stays between ¥157 and ¥158.5 while Tokyo's warnings cap gains and the Fed sets the tone.
scenarios.bull: A firm Fed lifts US yields and pushes the dollar toward ¥158.5, raising the odds that Tokyo acts.
scenarios.bear: A softer Fed, a stock sell-off or action from Tokyo sends the dollar back below ¥157.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc eased slightly, with the dollar near 0.830 francs, as calm markets kept demand for safety low. There was no Swiss news.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The franc is pulled between near-zero Swiss inflation, which keeps rates at zero, and its role as a safe place for money when markets are nervous. What changed: No Swiss data overnight; with Asian stocks rallying, the dollar edged up to near 0.8299 francs. What it means: Calm markets and zero Swiss rates give investors little reason to hold the franc. It would firm quickly if the Fed rattled markets or the Iran talks broke down. The question to keep asking: are markets nervous enough to seek safety?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: UBS's survey of Swiss economic expectations at 4:00 AM CT, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. The Swiss National Bank decides on December 10.

scenarios.base: The dollar stays between 0.825 and 0.833 francs while markets stay calm.
scenarios.bull: A firm Fed and steady stocks lift the dollar toward 0.835 francs.
scenarios.bear: A stock sell-off or failed Iran talks send money into the franc; the dollar slips below 0.825 francs.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: Australian inflation came in hotter than the Reserve Bank of Australia had forecast, making a rate hike on November 3 likely. The Aussie briefly rose above 70.5 US cents and settled near 70.35.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised rates four times this year as fuel costs from the Iran war push up prices, though a weak jobs market has made it unsure whether to go further. What changed: Underlying prices, measured by the trimmed mean that drops the biggest swings, rose 1.0% in the third quarter. That matched economists' forecasts but beat the bank's own 0.8% forecast; it works out to about 4% a year, above the 2–3% target. Headline prices rose 4.3% in the year to September, with petrol up sharply. Governor Michele Bullock told lawmakers inflation will likely run above the bank's forecast and that the board will debate next week whether four hikes are enough. Markets moved a November hike from roughly even odds to about 80%. What it means: Inflation running ahead of the bank's own path pushes it toward a fifth hike, and higher expected Australian rates support the Aussie. The weak jobs market is the main reason it could still wait. The question to keep asking: does the bank decide inflation needs one more hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Fed at 1:00 PM CT today, then Australian import prices at 7:30 PM CT tonight. The Reserve Bank of Australia decides on November 3.

scenarios.bull: A soft Fed on top of the hike bets lifts the Aussie above 70.6 cents.
scenarios.bear: A firm Fed lifts the US dollar broadly and drags the Aussie back below 70 cents.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie slipped to about 1.407 per US dollar before the Bank of Canada decision at 8:45 AM CT, even as oil rose. A hike is mostly expected, so what the bank signals about further moves matters most.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy has pushed Canadian inflation above the Bank of Canada's forecasts, so markets expect a rate hike today, which supports the loonie, while US tariffs still weigh on Canada's economy. What changed: No Canadian news overnight. US crude rose back above $101 a barrel, but the US dollar firmed against most currencies and ended Asia near 1.4066 Canadian. A hike to 2.50% is still priced at roughly 80%, though some big banks expect a hold. What it means: Most of a hike is already in the loonie's price. A hike with a hint of more would lift it, especially as hedge funds hold big bets against it; a hold would be the surprise and would hit it. New Zealand's surprise hold overnight is a reminder that a heavily priced hike is not guaranteed. The question to keep asking: does the bank hike and signal more?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report at 8:45 AM CT, Governor Tiff Macklem's press conference at 9:30 AM CT, then the Fed at 1:00 PM CT. Canada's August growth figures come on Friday.
numbers: Bank of Canada today: hike to 2.50% ~78–85%

scenarios.bull: A hike with a signal of more pushes the US dollar below 1.398 Canadian.
scenarios.bear: A hold surprises markets; the US dollar jumps above 1.415 Canadian.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand held rates at 2.75% when almost everyone expected a hike, and the kiwi fell as much as 1.7% to below 56 US cents. The bank still said more hikes are likely, so the move looks delayed, not dropped.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: New Zealand's central bank raised rates in July and September to fight fuel-driven inflation, and markets were almost sure of a third hike this week, which had kept the kiwi firm. What changed: The bank held at 2.75% in a 4–3 vote; most economists and about nine in ten market bets had expected a rise to 3%. Governor Anna Breman and the majority wanted to see how earlier hikes are working, but all seven members agreed further tightening is likely. The kiwi fell as much as 1.7% to about $0.558, then recovered to near $0.5606, and it lost ground against the Aussie too. What it means: The priced-in hike was taken out of the kiwi in one move. Because the bank kept the door open, the kiwi's next step depends on whether markets come to see December as a likely hike; until then, New Zealand rates sit below what investors expected. Hedge funds were already betting against the kiwi, and the hold paid them. The question to keep asking: does the bank make December a firm hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Fed at 1:00 PM CT today and ANZ's business confidence survey at 7:00 PM CT tonight. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand next decides on December 9, with a full policy statement.

scenarios.bear: A firm Fed or talk of a longer pause sends the kiwi below the overnight low near 55.8 cents.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil rose again in Asia, with Brent up about 1.3% to near $115 and US crude above $101, as hopes for the Iran talks faded. Saudi Arabia has still not confirmed a Houthi claim to have hit its biggest refinery.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, attacks on Gulf oil sites and shipping near the Strait of Hormuz have kept oil high, which lifts inflation everywhere and helps oil exporters like Canada. What changed: Brent rose about $1.50 to near $115.36 and US crude to about $101.12 in early Asian trading, reversing part of Tuesday's $2 fall. The Houthis' claim of a missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery is still unconfirmed, and no export disruption has been reported. Industry figures from the American Petroleum Institute showed a second weekly fall in US crude stocks. What it means: The market is still swinging between hope for a deal and fear of supply damage, so the war premium stays in the price. Higher oil keeps inflation pressure on central banks and is a cost for energy importers like Japan and the euro area. The question to keep asking: do the talks with Iran produce terms?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US government crude stock figures at 9:30 AM CT today, then the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, where output targets are expected to stay unchanged. Any confirmed damage at Ras Tanura or news from the Iran talks will move prices first.
numbers: API US crude stocks −2.0M barrels (second weekly fall)

scenarios.bull: Confirmed damage at Ras Tanura or a breakdown in talks sends Brent above $118.
scenarios.bear: Concrete terms from Iran lead to a deal outline; Brent falls toward $108.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold held above $4,000 an ounce overnight, near $4,050 in early trading, as the Fed decision approached. A firm signal on a December hike would weigh on it; a softer one would help.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold hit records earlier this month, then fell about 4% last week as the Federal Reserve signalled more rate rises to fight inflation near 3.7%. What changed: Gold, which dipped to $4,000 on Tuesday before buyers stepped in, traded near $4,051 early Wednesday with the dollar steady and US 10-year yields near 5%. What it means: Higher expected US rates make a metal that pays no interest less attractive and push the dollar up, so the Fed's message today is the main driver. Higher oil and the unresolved Iran talks keep some safety demand underneath. The question to keep asking: does the Fed sound firm enough on December to break $4,000?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: the Fed at 1:00 PM CT and Warsh's press conference at 1:30 PM CT, then US third-quarter growth and the Fed's preferred inflation measure at 7:30 AM CT Thursday.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
